text: Morrison Street is two-lane local road with a sidewalk on the north side and a speed limit of 50 km/hr. It meets other local roads at thirteen intersections, between Second and Thirteenth Streets, alternating between two-way and four-way stop controls. There are residences and school bus stops on both Morrison Street and its cross-streets. My office has requested traffic studies for four-way stop controls and almost every aforementioned intersection. Anecdotal reports from area residents suggests there is significant confusion and ambiguity for both vehicles and pedestrians traveling through the area with regards to traffic management controls along Morrison. I hereby request a traffic study on Morrison Street, in the area between Second Street and Thirteenth Street, to determine if any stop signs, or other traffic management methods are warranted for improved clarity and safety.

Etobicoke York Community Council: 1. Requested the Director, Transportation Services, Etobicoke York District, to undertake a traffic study on Morrison Street, between Second Street and Thirteenth Street, to determine if any stop signs or other traffic management devices are warranted to improve traffic flow and safety and for both vehicles and pedestrians.
